Beautiful yet corrosive liquid splashed across their armor. White smoke rose as chaos broke out. "Catch that damn Ava!" the governor shouted helplessly. But a swift figure had already appeared before him. In that moment, he finally saw the graffiti hero feared by villains—a cute girl with two large buns. Then a surge of paint flooded his vision… The next day, in the town square, the governor woke up at the busiest crossroads—painted into a clown. Around him, graffiti exposed how he had betrayed the town and exploited its people for years. Every passerby cursed the beast in human skin and cheered for the mysterious graffiti hero. In the crowd, Ava smiled with satisfaction. She had lost count of how many villains she had punished. There will always be dark corners in this world—and she will paint them all with her dual guns. "Who will be the next lucky one to receive my masterpiece? Could it be you, my dear governor?"

legacy:live:hero:charles:heroes.title: Charles
legacy:live:hero:charles:heroes.description: When Charles was born, the entire kingdom celebrated. The aging king finally had a son and adored him deeply, naming him heir at an early age. If nothing went wrong, Charles would become the youngest king in the kingdom's history. To make him a worthy ruler, countless masters trained him from childhood, teaching him day and night. Charles did not disappoint. He completed nearly every lesson perfectly, raising expectations for the young prince even higher. Charles had a secret he never told anyone—he didn't like this life at all. He didn't want to be king. Compared to dull lessons, he preferred staying in his room, secretly working on his inventions, like the piloted mech he was recently building. He always dreamed that once the mech was complete, he would ride it out of the palace and head somewhere far and free. And this time, he would never come back to this boring kingdom. The mech was soon complete, and the perfect chance to escape appeared. A neighboring kingdom, long at odds with them, suddenly invaded. Chaos spread everywhere—no one would notice him. Charles seized the moment and drove his mech along a route he had practiced countless times. On the way, he saw the teacher he once hated, now standing before enemies to protect civilians. The old butler, who used to stop every few steps to catch his breath, was now fighting with a weapon. The shopkeeper who always gave him snacks lay trembling on the ground… "What does it have to do with me? I finally got my freedom…" Charles muttered inside the mech. Bang! Enemy soldiers were sent flying. A massive figure landed before the invading army. "What is that monster?" Panic spread through their ranks, while cheers erupted in the capital. "It's the prince! He's here to save us!" With Charles leading, the kingdom's army surged with morale. With the mech clearing the way, the tide of battle quickly turned. In less than half a day, the invaders were driven back."Long live the prince!" Wherever Charles went, he was met with cheers. The once dull capital now seemed brighter in his eyes. The palace, once a cage, now felt warm and welcoming. "Maybe this place isn't so bad after all. I'll stay a little longer." That night, with a faint smile, Charles drifted into a peaceful sleep.

legacy:live:hero:wee-woo:heroes.title: Wee & Woo
legacy:live:hero:wee-woo:heroes.description: If you can't tell Wee from Woo, then the one standing next to Wee is Woo, and the one next to Woo is Wee. Still can't tell? Well, it doesn't really matter. They're always together. You'll rarely see them alone. People natu Rally treat them as one person. Twins this in sync are rare—eating together, sleeping together, being silly together… even going to war together. When Wee & Woo enter the battlefield, they become a nightmare. No one can lock onto them. All you see is a nimble cannon roaming the field, firing powerful shells from every direction, crushing both enemy formations and their hope. "Woo is the smartest person in the world! Ever since we were kids, he's always scored full marks! And he invents amazing things—like this cannon we're using now. He designed and improved it all by himself. Me? I just help out… Anyway, Woo is a genius!" Whenever someone asks Wee about Woo, he can go on praising him for days, completely ignoring Woo blushing beside him. "Wee is amazing. He's strong and fast, unlike me… He's also really brave. Whenever there's danger, he steps forward first, unlike me… And he's kind. If someone needs help, he'll always be there, unlike me… Wee is the best person in the world!" Shy Woo only becomes this talkative when speaking about Wee. At those moments, Wee always looks at him with gentle eyes. "I don't want to be with you anymore!" No one knows who said it first, but Wee & Woo did separate once. "Without me holding him back, he'll have an easier life." They both thought the same thing. For a while after that, they lived on their own. Without Wee, Woo struggled to move his equipment. He couldn't even speak up when buying supplies, and his experiments came to a halt. Without Woo, Wee clumsily fixed his armor and counted expenses on his fingers, turning his home into a mess. "I can't live without Wee (Woo)." In the end, they went back to being inseparable, as if nothing had ever happened.

legacy:live:hero:yang:heroes.title: Yang
legacy:live:hero:yang:heroes.description: In the frozen wilds, " Yang" is more than just a name. It's a legend carried on every icy wind. They call her the "Winter Huntress," and her reputation echoes across the endless snowfields. People trust Yang, not only because she can track any beast or find her way through the worst storms, but because she never loses her head, no matter how dire things get. In a crisis, she's the first to take charge. Whether it's finding shelter, reading the winds, or building a fire, she's always steady and never rattled. Even when danger closes in, she makes tough calls without hesitation, calmly organizing everyone's escape. The harsh polar climate hasn't worn her down. If anything, it's made her even more clearheaded and unshakable under pressure. But don't mistake her for some grim, silent type. Yang has a mischievous streak. She'll crack a joke around the campfire or build a goofy snowman with her board just to get a laugh. Her chilly sense of humor is legendary, and her jokes help keep everyone's spirits up, even in the coldest nights. She knows better than anyone that out here, losing your nerve is far more dangerous than any blizzard. A century ago, the polar regions were just a distant frontier. A cold land, yes, but they were home to thriving communities. The royal oracles once urged the kingdom's fleets to sail north, and for many years, the two lands built strong ties by sharing supplies and aid. Those were prosperous times, with endless convoys heading into the snow. But one fateful day, a fleet found its way blocked by shifting ice. Only then did people realize a terrible storm had struck the polar lands. Seas froze, the cold deepened, and entire villages vanished beneath the snow. Thankfully, those earlier alliances helped some survive. But soon, the polar seas were sealed in ice, cutting off all travel and trade. Years later, when the ice finally began to thaw, a group journeyed south, only to find the kingdom gone. Rebels had torn it apart. Royal bloodlines were scattered and forced to live in hiding. The crown was lost, but the burden of old grudges remained. That night, the elders of the polar lands gathered in secret. After a long, heavy silence, they made their choice: someone must go and seek out the last of the royal line. Oh, how the bards love to sing of her, lutes in hand, in the dusky twilight. "Winter mountain sent, Boots of snow, Not knowing which way to go, Told by stars where to follow, Oh, the road is long, But still she must sing on and on. North wind blowing, Bonfire sowing, Lost footprints flowing, 'Till she knew where she was going. Oh, to raise a glass to hope, To laugh as long as winter's snow, 'Til she knows which way to go, Joined to a fantasy that never overflows, goes or slows... The wind still howled outside, the fire crackled in the darkness. Yang packed her things for the journey, fumbling with the straps, clearly lost in thought. "The place you're headed won't be any kinder than these frozen plains," the elder said softly. "Right now, you don't seem like the legendary Huntress. What's troubling you?" Yang looked up. "...I worry that if things are too different out there, I'll end up changing too much..." The elder pulled his coat tighter, a gentle smile on his face. "There's nothing wrong with change. Life's a voyage, and every sea you cross leaves its mark on your ship. To keep going, you patch it up and sail on." He looked Yang in the eye. "When friends drift away, you learn to take the first step. When family tests your patience, you learn to stand on your own. When no one seems to notice your efforts, you start to doubt yourself." Yang sat in silence. The elder poked the fire, making the flames leap higher. "But what makes a ship itself isn't the wood it's built from, but that it always knows where it's headed." Outside, the storm still raged. Yang fastened her board to her pack, her eyes full of resolve. The path to legend was waiting, and she was ready to face it.

legacy:live:hero:triton:heroes.title: Triton
legacy:live:hero:triton:heroes.description: Triton is a Generation 6 SSR hero in Kingshot, belonging to the Infantry class. He can be obtained through the Hall of Heroes and the Sacred Sword Shop.

legacy:live:hero:sophia:heroes.title: Sophia
legacy:live:hero:sophia:heroes.description: Nightfall could not hide the magnificence of the approaching envoy. All eyes were transfixed by the four great horses pulling a mighty black carriage. Whatever dark pigments used to achieve the effect must be rather remarkable. It did not resemble black paint so much as a portal into absolute darkness, by which no light was reflected on its dark exterior. Once arrived, the occu Pant of the stately carriage stepped down with a deep sigh. The villagers continued to stare—a noble lady, no doubt, whose beautiful dark dress and bodice contrasted brilliantly with her albino-white skin. The magnificent red hair above her shoulders and hat to which a scarlet rose was pinned only added to the dramatic entrance. She regarded the crowd with a certain coolness that was not totally without warmth. And when she spoke, the crowd hung on to her every husky word. The few guardsmen that accom Panied the carriage was hardly an escort of honor. Besides, how had they managed to carve a path through the rebellious areas full of strife and civil war without a brigade of soldiers? Such questions could be asked later. What mattered now was this ambassadorial envoy had arrived and the great welcome feast would shortly begin. "You should know that marrying me has a cost you may not want to pay in the fullness of time..." The Count loved speaking in such riddles. His wise manner and deep voice seemed out-of-place for his youthful appearance. "I will go to the ends of the earth with you." Sophia gazed lovingly at the handsome man across from her, not a shred of doubt in her voice. She had cast aside all rumors when pursuing him. His pallid-white face that never seemed to see the sun was no obstacle either. Instead, she loved his rosy red lips, the cultured hands that excited her so much when they tapped her on the shoulder, and his dark eyes full of mystery. In the end Sophia obtained the prize that she wanted: marriage to the Count and a new life as his Countess. She didn't want to spoil the occasion of their magnificent wedding by questioning why the ceremony and banquet had to be conducted at night, nor the strangeness of the enormous crowd of new faces, odd music, and reliance on candlelight. She was with her husband now. She was determined to overlook anything else. If Sophia had not been head over heels for the Count, she might have taken the time to reflect on the peculiar absence of mirrors in his villa or why she never saw any of his friends during the day. Nor did she seem to notice the eerie smiles, the grins from ear to ear that lit up guests' faces from out of the corner of her eyes. Truly Sophia's heart had chosen for her that night. And this decision could never be changed. The village's troubles began only a few hours after Countess Sophia's arrival. The town had taken in an enormous number of vagabonds, refugees, and miscreants in recent years, but had placed them all outside the city limits and the protection of the law. This camp meant to give hope to the hopeless was ruled by an Iron-fisted, cruel man. His abuses seemed to imply he had forgotten that at one point he had been a refugee himself. He used the camp's disorder to work with rebels from outside for his and their enrichment. The only thing the sentry saw in the fading light was a strange rose on the wind. But he had no time to marvel. As soon as the rose touched his skin, he stumbled. And then, shaking and shivering, stood up again and walked with dogged determination into the center of camp. Soon after the entire camp, was wakened by the screams of horses and people fleeing from fire within. But only the veterans recognized the true nature of their emergency—the horrible crackling of fire intermingled with swords slicing flesh. The fire raged long and hard that night. Barely any of the camp remained next morning. Shortly before sunrise, the lady in black who had so enchanted the crowds walked out. No one saw her. She still had in her eyes the same cruelty, yet somehow her makeup was also smudged by red tears streaming down her cheeks. She was holding the rose, the source of so much trouble. The red-blood of the rose was a fine match for what it had wrought that night. It glowed eerily. Immortality is the greatest punishment ever visited upon mortal-kind. Endless life seems to provide the freedom to wait and to hope—to live adventurously and love boldly. But who will be there for you after inevitability takes away all the wonderfulness that you have so carefully crafted? You will soon learn to recognize the passions of your mortal body for what they truly are: daggers meant to strike your heart when most vulnerable. Everyone on this journey begins by a different road, but all roads lead to the same destination. Get used to seeing everyone you once loved taken by Father Time. And then you too will be taken—that is, your glorious radiant heart that lives and loves and overflows with passion. So goes the author's famous introduction to immortality from the adventure novel "Four Hundred Years of Solitude". Derided by some prominent town critics as "so much trash", it is hard to deny his realistic treatment of immortality's consequences stirred the imaginations of many readers. The alleged inspiration for this novel? A chance meeting between author, governor, and a mysterious Countess Sophia.

legacy:live:hero:vivian:heroes.title: Vivian
legacy:live:hero:vivian:heroes.description: Vivian is a Mythic-quality Generation 5 Hero in Kingshot, classified under the Archer class. You can unlock her through the Hall of Heroes and Swordland Showdown Shop.

legacy:live:hero:thrud:heroes.title: Thrud
legacy:live:hero:thrud:heroes.description: "Here lies one born in war." Baptized by thunder Bathed in blood and broken bones; Here lies one born of glory. Songbringer in the storm. Upon which enemies tremble and gnash their teeth; For whom the Golden Gates stand open. Until stars fall and sea overcomes land." ——Eternal Warrior, Thrud the Wolf-Kissed What can one say about Thrud and Helga that hasn't already been said? Of their different temperaments it is known. Of Thrud's rashness and impulsiveness, love of wine and addiction to battle it is legendary. Well told are the stories around the Northland inns of Thrud the Great. It is well-known that her weapons of choice are twin axes, which she can throw at a moment's notice. Her choice of adornment is also noteworthy—a beautiful white direwolf coat, said to be a former com Panion who died at her side, spoken by some as a lost descendant of the great Fenrir who comes to her aid in battle. Well known is the honorific given to Thrud, the " Wolf-Kissed". For she has "kissed" wolves and death many times. Thrud is a warrior of warriors but even she has served under greater legends, like the once great chief of chiefs Ivar Ironfist. A long time ago, before Ivar's sun had set and hair turned gray, Thrud was no more than a common soldier under his watch. Those were great days of pillaging! Plundering! Many towns were razed. Many gasps were uttered at the sight of the infamous longship of dread that brought screams and bitter nights. It was inevitable that deadly ambition would creep in to the purity of their swords as the plunder of the clan grew. One wrong move and any chieftain can lose everything. A new breed of warriors ascended the stage and cast out the old chiefs. The fate of a retired Viking Lord is sad indeed. Death in battle is far preferred to becoming a laughing stock of the able-bodied. Unworthy to be slain in battle, old Vikings frequently become nomads, shaking their fists at daily disrespect. "I'll give you an honorable death! Rise, Ivar Ironfist!" Thrud spoke in a low voice, "Come fight your finest duel with me! Should the gates of Valhalla be opened to one such as Ivar who had not the pleasure of dying on the battlefield? The old man's dry eyes could have wept for joy at the thought he would finally be released into Valhalla's glory. Red was the sword that delivered him from the earth. And joyous was the heart of the man who died. "Upon the shore of the Western Sea stood row upon row of Iron shields. Waves of our warriors were beaten back, spears splintered, legs and arms heavy with wounds. Our men looked at each other in fear and trembling, and then... then Thrud appeared." She had no speech to give, but lifting twin axes in twin hands, charged into the fray. Can you imagine? One woman against that wall? The laughter of the enemy soon turned to screams. The battle lines began to shake! Blue light flashed here and there... What was it now?! A great white wolf! Fenrir had heard the cry of Thrud and come to her aid!" "The enemy ranks broke! They fled! And everyone knew, crystal clear, who in that moment had delivered them, who had saved the Viking army from ruin!" Another colorful story of great deeds in battle told beautifully by Jaeger to the assembled. They looked to Helga occasionally to see in her eyes whether it was true. She had been there. But she only smiled from the door, content to keep her counsel secret.

legacy:live:hero:longfei:heroes.title: Long Fei
legacy:live:hero:longfei:heroes.description: Long Fei is a Mythic-quality Generation 5 hero in Kingshot, classified under the Infantry class. You can unlock him through the Hero Roulette and Swordland Showdown Shop.

legacy:live:hero:rosa:heroes.title: Rosa
legacy:live:hero:rosa:heroes.description: Rosa is an incredibly charming lady. Her eyes hold the depth of a starry sky, and her dance moves leave everyone enthralled. According to those who have analyzed Rosa's performance, she possesses an incredible sense of rhythm, with passionate and bold movements. By skillfully playing with light reflected from the mirrors, she effortlessly commands the spotlight on the tavern stage. The mix of all these elements blows the audience away. Before they even realize it, Rosa has already stolen their hearts. Smith, a regular at the tavern and a part-time writer in town, once put into words the people's admiration for Rosa: "Tonight, I whisper to you, my beautiful muse. You've stirred my heart, and blurred my gaze. The thoughts I hold deep within, I dare not let escape my lips." As the tavern's star, Rosa's performances never fail to dazzle the audience. But when the curtain falls, she becomes a different person—her eyes grow distant and icy like a glacier, driving away anyone who tries to approach her. On a fateful night, rebels stormed the town, driving helpless residents to pray in their cellars. Even seasoned guards trembled under the enemy's relentless as Sault, yet Rosa stood tall, ascending the city walls. Without the lute's song, she danced to the thunderous crash of catapults. Her bloodstained dress whipped like a battle flag through the smoke, inspiring everyone to fight with renewed courage. A stitched journal lies open at the center of the table, its cover bound in an unusual leather, the corners worn pale with age. The text on the left side of the cover is blurred, but a few words remain barely legible. "To... my dearest..." The text on the right is clearer. "If separation was written in our fate, why were our paths made to cross at all?" "Perhaps nothing in this world truly holds meaning. But if I must give our encounter one, then let the part of me you changed remain by my side, in your place—forever." Faint, round blotches mark the corners of the paper as if something had dampened it. A door opened, and the tavern's biggest star stepped into the warmth of her home.

legacy:live:hero:margot:heroes.title: Margot
legacy:live:hero:margot:heroes.description: A Mythic-grade Generation 4 Cavalry hero in Kingshot. Obtainable via Hall of Heroes and the Swordland Showdown Shop.

legacy:live:hero:alcar:heroes.title: Alcar
legacy:live:hero:alcar:heroes.description: Alcar was once a member of the Praetorian Guard. More precisely, he held the prestigious title of " Flagbearer," a rank reserved for the cream of the crop. Ordinary citizens might not fully grasp the significance of this title, which signifies absolute strength and unwavering loyalty. It is an exceptional honor earned through fierce competition among the legions. Among all the Praetorian Guards, there can be only one Flagbearer. "Surrender is never an option! We do not retreat, we do not yield! Raise your weapons! This is loyalty to the Emperor, this is a Vow of Honor!" Alcar once declared. "We're an impregnable force, standing steadfast at the frontlines." "We embody courage and the victory." "We shall protect the Emperor, even at the cost of our lives!" Time and again, Alcar revisited the moment he was appointed Flagbearer in his dreams, only to be pulled back to reality by the biting cold of the wintry night. At the sound of hurried footsteps, he instinctively tightened his grip on his weapon... "They only send us because they think there's no chance of winning! You need to know that, Alcar!" "Exactly! I'm sure the empire's already a lost cause!" "I don't believe it... His Majesty wouldn't just stand by and watch this happen..." "For heaven's sake, where's the Emperor now?! The empire's a gone case, and the power's fallen into other hands." "We have to win this impossible battle to have a chance to see His Majesty." "But..." "I'm b Egging you, Alcar. I know this is tough, but that's the reason we're sent here..." Alcar couldn't remember who convinced him to fight back then. The Empire's fate seemed to have nothing to do with the Praetorian Guards, who lived by loyalty, but at that moment, none of it mattered anymore... Alcar endures the agony of surviving while his comrades fell and the torment of betraying his own beliefs. When he removes his armor, it reveals a body marked by scars—not only from the battles he survived but also from the pain he inflicted upon himself in his search for redemption. Now, this former Flagbearer has been given a new lease on life in this small town. His past fame no longer binds him. "I've long given up on changing the world. Now, I only strive to stay true to myself,' he said.

legacy:live:hero:jaeger:heroes.title: Jaeger
legacy:live:hero:jaeger:heroes.description: Kingshot Gen 3 SSR Archer hero Jaeger can be obtained through Daily Deals, Hero Rally, Swordland Shop, and the Strongest Governor Event.

legacy:live:hero:eric:heroes.title: Eric
legacy:live:hero:eric:heroes.description: In a past life Eric was called "The Pious One" for his unshakable willingness to use the paladin's hammer of correction against any entity willing to slander or harm the Ecclesia, its reputation, or property. A firm believer in the notion that "whoever is not absolutely loyal to us is against us", Eric gladly accepted whatever task the Ecclesia assigned, even the oftentimes unpleasant business of forced tithing. Eric was an absolutist in principle, unmoved by the flattery of a nobleman's words or pleas of the landholder. The 10% mandatory tithe was to be paid by hook or by crook, nothing more and certainly nothing less. It was a job that required a forceful personality. Unbelievably, the Ecclesia's subjects would occasionally object to the levy. On those days it helped that Eric could take his hammer and smash open whatever their secret storehouse owed. Ever loyal, Eric would most likely have perished on some far-flung battlefield in defense of the church had not his path in life forked down a particularly dramatic mission—the failed tithe that led to his current situation. Eric's final levy was of a prosperous town under the protective radiance of the Ecclesia. What greeted Eric's eyes there was nothing like the description he had been given, but a shanty village r Avaged by disease, blighted by bandits, and starved from poor harvests. Yet an edict was an edict. Eric had faith enough to carry out some sort of levy on peasants who would have trouble enough surviving winter as it was. Eric's fair implementation of the levy meant collecting significantly less food than the Ecclesia had hoped. He received their reply at the next waypost: the small amount of grain did not to justify the costs of transportation. It was all to be burned so Eric can immediately head for a more prosperous town. Eric could hardly believe his eyes. The peasants' life-giving grain was to be burned? Eric decided to pause his trip until his heart could find its place again. Fortunately for Eric and unfortunately for the Ecclesia, it was around this time that he came into contact with Hilde who had been passing out food to help with the famine. Eric was shocked to learn Hilde had begun working for the Ecclesia after her parents had sold her into slavery as a young girl because they could not meet the minimum tithing requirement. Hilde's tale broke something inside Eric. Eric re-emerged from his quarters after a day of quiet meditation to announce he was no longer a Paladin of the Light, but a "dark hammer" for breaking chains of oppression. Eric's hammer is now directed at a very different kind of correction: the rectification by blunt force of evil hypocrites.

legacy:live:hero:petra:heroes.title: Petra
legacy:live:hero:petra:heroes.description: Kingshot Gen 3 SSR Cavalry hero. Obtainable from the Hero Roulette and Swordland Showdown.

legacy:live:hero:hilde:heroes.title: Hilde
legacy:live:hero:hilde:heroes.description: Hilde, born into a noble family, was sent to a church for education at a young age due to certain family reasons. Hilde had her happiest childhood memories there, always able to find joy in the otherwise dull and somber life at the church. Her cheerful presence brought a spark of light to the austere lives of the priests. Unfortunately, Hilde was struck by a hereditary eye disease at fourteen. This strange illness would eventually take away the patient's sight. Some in Hilde's family lost their vision in a few short years, while others only suffered the ordeal decades later. However, blindness was inescapable, unless a miracle happened... Hilde was still able to see when she first contracted the disease. Upon learning that it would take at least a few years for her disease to progress, she decided to make a prayer. Through her devotion, she received a divine revelation: to study pharmacology. It was a trial she had to conquer to restore her vision. From then on, Hilde dedicated herself to studying her eye disease day and night, praying for a miracle. The others at the temple intended to persuade Hilde to accept her fate, but none dared to defy the divine revelation... Perhaps it was the power of the miracle, or maybe Hilde was truly a genius, but against all odds, her eye disease surprisingly slowed its progression, allowing her to retain some of her sight. Intrigued by Hilde's story, an archbishop of the church invited her to join the central cathedral and study alongside him. Unfortunately, beneath the archbishop's seemingly kind gesture lay a sinister motive—to study Hilde's cursed eyes and offer them to a powerful figure. The archbishop cruelly took Hilde's eyes under the guise of a baptism ceremony and used his influence to cover up the truth. Meanwhile, Hilde's family had long given up on her due to the eye disease. No one cared about her fate... Hilde once recounted the miracle that occurred to her. A sound in her mind guided her back to consciousness, and to her surprise, she could perceive everything happening around her when she woke up... Hilde called this ability the "spiritual sight." It is hard to believe that a blind monk can live a normal life, but those who have been helped by Hilde see her as the embodiment of compassion. Not only does she offer guidance to the lost through her devout prayers, but she also uses her medical knowledge to heal the world.

legacy:live:hero:zoe:heroes.title: Zoe
legacy:live:hero:zoe:heroes.description: Zoe manifests her emotional states not through words or actions, but through her magical hair... According to Amadeus, her hair has reflected her mood since she was young. While black signifies her patience as she waits to strike at her prey, yellow reflects her exhilaration as she starts hunting. Zoe channels the energy of every cell in her body to chase down her prey, ultimately tearing them apart. Zoe isn't a noble knight or an elegant archer, but an adopted child of the Unjust League just like Amadeus. Born with immense strength, Zoe always charges to the frontline of battles, relishing the exhilaration each wound brings and taking pleasure in raw, physical contact. Ruthless in her attacks, Zoe is willing to go to any lengths to secure victory, even if it means being seen as a villain. To her, winning is everything, and honor holds little value. Zoe was raised in a suburban area north of Noxholm, a region bordering a forest and home to the destitute. Yet, even there, Zoe wasn't spared from the exorbitant taxes, the nobles who tormented the common folk for amusement, and the fanatical cults eager to spread their influence. She also witnessed countless betrayals and backstabbing, even within families. The underprivileged, regarded as insignificant by the nobility, were willing to pay any price just to survive another day. It was in this harsh reality that Zoe realized the necessity of becoming stronger—so she could call the shots in this unforgiving society and one day obliterate everything that stood against her beliefs. Zoe is infamous for getting into bar brawls, being one of the top troublemakers at the Adventurers' Camp, and using underhanded tactics to snatch bounty Missions. She's become the town's bogeyman—mothers often use her name to scare unruly children into behaving. But despite her rough reputation, Zoe has earned a great deal of respect and admiration. She's won "Best Vanguard Captain" and "Best Adventure Com Panion" multiple times at the camp, and she's even the female lead in a Romance novel written by bestselling author Smith. In his book, Fluttering Heart, there's a line that says, "The lady is like a rainbow—you only believe such beauty exists when you see it." It’s a sentiment that captures how those who admire Zoe truly feel.

legacy:live:hero:marlin:heroes.title: Marlin
legacy:live:hero:marlin:heroes.description: Even someone as calm and steady as Forrest often wonders how the large ship from the north suddenly appeared in town. Its hull is riddled with dents of varying sizes, and a massive tear stretches from the center to the bow, as though it had been pierced by some enormous, sharp object. Whenever a curious child or nosy villager approached, they would invariably be chased away by an elderly man wearing a black tricorn and a red woolen coat. One day, the mystery of the vessel was finally solved when the Well-Traveled Quinn recognized it as "The Santiago," a ship that had been missing for thirty years. The drunken old man turned out to be Captain Marlin, once one of the Four Great Captains. In his prime, Marlin commanded nearly ten ships and had almost a thousand sailors under his command. His remarkable success earned him the title of one of the Four Great Captains from the royal court. Feeling on top of the world, Marlin decided to lead his formidable fleet into an uncharted sea and had a sailor send out one final letter to the world, as his usual practice. "The Waters before us seem calm, but I sense there is more to them than meets the eye. Be prepared, everyone! May glory be with the Santiago." This crumpled letter remains in the royal library to this day. Marlin and his fleet vanished into thin air for a full 30 years, and no one knows what became of them. The area where Marlin disappeared became known as the Misty Tides, as it was perpetually shrouded in dense fog. From time to time, thrill-seekers braved its Waters, hoping to unravel the mystery of the lost fleet. Yet, they all shared the same tragic fate, becoming yet another chapter in the haunting legend of this sea... In response to the rising number of casualties, the royal court issued a decree banning entry to the area to avoid causing widespread Panic. News of the strange event eventually reached even the inland towns. Some call the region the "Demon's Delta," while others describe it as a gateway to the underworld—after all, no one has ever returned alive from those cursed Waters. "There's nothing there. Ever heard of sea fog? It forms when cold air meets warm air..." "Burp... Why won't it clear up, you ask? You know anything about the magnetic fields? Well, the magnetic field there's all messed up, and it's trapping the fog. Burp—we were stuck there too..." "We must believe in science! There's no such thing as demons!" The old drunkard did his best to explain science to the other patrons at the bar, but even with his neck turning red, he couldn't get his message through. The crowd dispersed, realizing there was no juicy story. The once-clamorous bar fell quiet again, with only the old drunkard remaining. "Demons? Burp... If there were one, my buddies and I would have already taken care of it. It wouldn't have had a chance to survive..."

legacy:live:hero:jabel:heroes.title: Jabel
legacy:live:hero:jabel:heroes.description: Jabel's early life was shaped by tragedy. Only she escaped the terrible bandit attack that destroyed her village. The details of her life between that fateful night and the day she became a paladin are hazy. But she has never wavered from her life's motto: "Never fear darkness. Fear only the despair of the faithless." The red-armored c Avalrywoman and her lance have travelled many kingdoms. By her perseverance she has encouraged governors; helped the struggling. She has worked always to remind people to hope for a more glorious turn of history's page. "My child, in this world you will see many things. It is not always easy to tell who is good and who is bad. But no matter who you meet... Remember what I always told you." Jabel's elderly father has a haunting look in his eyes, a kindly man with wisps of gray hair. "Defeat is temporary. True despair is only felt in the absence of Conviction and heart." As her father always said these words, Jabel has always memorized them. "The Holy Ecclesia has given me a mission. I must go. There may be troubles on the way... as at home. Look after your mother and yourself. Be here and be safe when I come home. Will you do that for me?" This memory burns like ice. Jabel snaps back to reality. She must have drunk too much that evening. She shakes it off. Then lies down again against the city wall. Jabel's father Aman attained to the rank of Paladin in the Holy Ecclesia, charged with keeping members of the flock safe. It was a job which earned the family great respect in the village. The beginning of the troubles began with Cesares' rebellion and his seizure of the Citadel. The church changed too. Gentle doctrine was discarded. Paladins begun to seize the assets of the faithful. Oppressed by the king on the one hand and on the other hand by the church, the community took out their anger on Jabel and her mom in their father's absence. Jabel's father returned home after many trials, but the sight of their home chilled him to his core. He could not tell who had done it—the Rebels, the church itself, or bandits. Smoke from the village filled the air. Blood flowed in the streets, swallowing up any hope of ever rebuilding... "Not all who sit upon horses are paladins. Not all who wear armor stand with Conviction. I have seen the faithful sacrifice themselves for one another. I have seen nobles take pleasure in bullying the weak. We must never judge the content of another's character by the circumstances of their birth." "It is only faith, only the purity of Conviction, only idealism, that which you are willing to die for, that makes a person great and a true paladin." "Be prepared to use the rest of your life to find your sacred light. Even if you must fight in a world full of chaos and pain. Are you willing? Even to death?" These words are etched by the entrance of the Imperial museum by the First Paladin of the Imperial C Avalry: Jabel.

legacy:live:hero:amadeus:heroes.title: Amadeus
legacy:live:hero:amadeus:heroes.description: Amadeus is an incredible swordsman in both speed and power. His twin swords are fast enough, some say, to split a river in two. That seems unbelievable until you witness him for yourself. On the outside, Amadeus is quiet. Rough. But underneath his dark exterior lies a heart of gold. Perhaps because Amadeus' adoptive father understood that about him so well that he was allowed Amadeus to accom Pany him on his outlaw adventures. While Amadeus' advice may be unreliable, his swordsmanship never let the League down. Amadeus' strengths would soon be put to the test in unfamiliar territory: town. He is stopped immediately by Jabel, a c Avalrywoman shocked he would enter so openly with a bounty on his head. And also that such a bounty could lie on the head of one so young. But Amadeus was determined. Duty was calling. The air became thick with the possibility of a fight... until someone finally intervened. A great shield between the two defused the tension at last. The group that Amadeus had been part of through his father is the "Unjust League", widely condemned as a criminal organization. Its leader, "Robin Hood", is regarded as an outlaw, particularly by the nobility for his fondness for robbing the wealthy. That is what the townsfolk found so intriguing about Amadeus' openness. There was a certain courage and honesty on the part of the young man. One might have expected such a notorious outlaw would be shunned. Yet the town cautiously welcomed him as he went about his day. For his part, Amadeus made sure any friendly service was met with equally friendly and prompt payment. What a surprise! Amadeus found himself wondering: Could this town be truly as wise and fair as they say? Perhaps there is an oasis to be carved out in this lawless world? "What do you think? If she's always coming up with reasons to bother you? If she's always finding excuses to watch you? I say it's very interesting. I say it's the hallmarks of a shy girl." But Quinn would always say that, the self-proclaimed warrior-poet and expert on love. Amadeus looked back at Quinn blankly. Quinn quickly added: "Think about it: a c Avalrywoman of principle. An outlaw with a heart of gold? Well? You two have promise." Meanwhile, Seth was furiously scribbling the conversation down in one of his diaries. Quinn's table conversation was interrupted by a flying pitcher. "I think we've all drunk enough for one evening, eh? Time for some fun." "Finally!" So another bar fight began.

legacy:live:hero:helga:heroes.title: Helga
legacy:live:hero:helga:heroes.description: Helga is an extraordinary figure. Long, gentle hair, fine clothing, and a soft voice indicates grace and refinement. Step onto the battlefield, and Helga's true nature emerges. She wields a long lance as sharp as any for tearing down defensive lines. On horseback, she presses enemies on wings of terror. If you are so unlucky as to become her enemy, pray that this Valkyrie may have mercy on your soul. Adventurer Quinn may be the only person in town who dares to call himself her equal (and coincidentally has made his feelings for her known countless times). Her rejections have driven him crazy. His latest musing? "I must see which of us is stronger, myself or Helga, on the battlefield or off it! Or I shall never depart this town!" Helga hails from a Viking tribe in the northlands. Her parents were well-respected warriors and she learned how to ride a moose even as a young girl. She had already showed great talent for combat at a young age, but also something else too: a refusal to accept the warlike ways of her ancestors. When hunting, Helga keenly felt that the beauty of nature and sanctity of life should not be disturbed lightly or easily. She began to doubt: how could anything be more important than living at peace with others? Helga's growing independence clashed frequently with tribal tradition. It was too much: constant plundering. Constant oppression. Helga's rage publicly exploded at the warchief one day after he announced a new campaign. It was a humiliation with a price to pay for both of them. Judgment was rendered against Helga: she would have to survive a duel to the death against the warchief's champion, the strongest of their tribe. It was supposed to be an execution. Helga surprised everyone by slaying their leader's anointed. Victory bought survival. She was allowed to leave on mooseback. So she left her only home and vanished from the tribe forevermore. Helga's act of rebellion stirred up something deep in the warchief's heart. What if Helga's resistance had been the start of a greater movement? Even the beginnings of a coup? If warriors were allowed to make their own decisions about when and where to go to war, then the authority of the warchief would come into question. Then it was only a matter of time until their tribe would be conquered by other Vikings with greater unity of purpose and turned into slaves. The warchief began a great cleansing after Helga's departure. Warriors who did not show absolute loyalty were driven out mercilessly. It took 10 years, but at the end the warchief was able to secure for himself the fearsome title of Viking King. Yet that one act of resistance from Helga still burns in the Viking King's heart. But wait, what news has the scout brought today? A familiar lady-warrior in traditional garb has just been sighted in the new lands? A new campaign, it seems, must soon begin.

legacy:live:hero:saul:heroes.title: Saul
legacy:live:hero:saul:heroes.description: Saul's constant grin can be unnerving. He smiles even when people reassure him it is not necessary. He smiles even when it seems forced. It is as if he is hiding something. But what? There's no one better when it comes to logistics than Saul. Need something built? Supplies gathered? Army provisions? Saul's your man. There is something driving him to work faster, harder, better. Few have asked why. In a world as broken as this, it is often better not to ask questions. Saul's past is tied to the Pilgrimage Alliance, a military organization under the old Royal Expeditionary Force. Although small, the Alliance was tasked with maintaining order at holy sites and protecting the faithful. But the Pilgrimage Alliance quickly swelled with recruits seeking refuge from the outside world. Rapid growth came with unchecked ambition. The king soon ordered their activities be drastically cut. Saul was then assigned to the Order of Holy Paladins under the Holy Ecclesia. This heavily-armed force was concerned with finding more holy relics for the church. Saul's unit was known as the "Wild Rabbit Brigade". The Wild Rabbits were missing for over a month when the worst time of Saul's life occurred. Saul saved his diary from those days. It traces the rough outline of the Wild Rabbits' journey to explore an ancient site called the Golden City. "This is our first week in the Golden City. The buildings are made out of solid gold! But apart from golden statues we have found nothing else of any value. This place is utterly desolate. But many of us are very excited at discovering gold. I'm sure these riches will help the mother church immensely!" "A second week of searching has turned up nothing except deep fissures where veins of pure gold glitter in the sunlight. Yet the sight of it leaves people sick and disorientated. The entire city is so quiet. It is eerie. We are still moving towards the center. There we can see a giant golden circular structure. I needn't add that we are on high alert. We've already had several desertions. Desertions... or something else?" "I know not what week it is. Most everyone is mad here. I'm probably mad too. What's the use of gold? We can't eat it. All that matters now is we cannot look at the great circular demon structure in the middle of the city! It is cursed. The Holy Mother protect me and watch over me. Protect me from the evil spirit that reigns in this city..." The last few pages of the journal are written in a barely-legible scrawl. "What else do I remember? Barely anything until Captain pulled me away from a great pile of gold... I think he saved my life." Saul spoke in a low voice as Seth kept jogging down notes in his little book. "What happened to the others?" Seth finally asked. "They became statues! My fate would have been the same had Captain not given me his face-shield. When that darned light hit our eyes... it couldn't reach me! The damned light! It shines into your soul!" Saul resumed after a brief silence, "I'll never forget the last thing Captain said to me: run! Forget this city! Forget any of this ever happened! Just smile! Smile because you lived!" Saul twisted his face into a nervous grin. The grin felt different. It was hard to make out other people's faces in the candlelight. How many drinkers at the inn were listening intently to Saul's story? What were they thinking? A great city full of gold? Potentially cursed? Perhaps they will fare better?

legacy:live:hero:amane:heroes.title: Amane
legacy:live:hero:amane:heroes.description: Standing on tiptoe, Amane glanced around the market in the unfamiliar city worlds apart from the life she once knew. In her haste, her wide sleeves nearly knocked over a fruit stall. "Oops, so sorry about that!" Clumsily, she gathered the fallen fruits and handed the vendor a candy as an apology. The vendors nearby, who found her behavior unusual, were all amused. As Amane awkwardly asked about the governor's whereabouts in broken local language, a group of children gathered around her, eager to guide her... and eyeing her candy at the same time. " Amane? She's holed up in her room again, poring over those strange symbols again!" Olive chuckled as she pushed open the door. Inside, Amane sat surrounded by ancient tomes and scattered papers covered in charms. Her hair was casually tied in a messy bun, and she was muttering to herself. Without looking up, Amane said, "Almost done! Just need to add a few more strokes..." Those "few strokes" ended up taking the whole day. It wasn't until her stomach started growling in the evening that she finally came out to grab a bite. On her way to the kitchen, she slipped a freshly drawn amulet to the elderly lady next door, who suffered from insomnia. On a distant island, there is a legend of a divine tree at the place closest to the sky. Its trunk is said to hold a power capable of restoring life. Devoted shrine maidens dedicate their entire lives seeking this divine tree, hoping to craft an amulet that protects all creatures from war, disease, and disaster. Unfortunately, no one has found the tree in centuries, and its existence has faded into myth. When the elderly deacon placed the revitalizing amulet in the palm of the injured person, a miracle took place. The wound healed quickly, the breathing steadied, and an invisible force held the god of death at bay. "He's saved!" He's awake! Unbelievable!" the onlookers exclaimed. Without a word, the elderly deacon motioned for the others to tend to the injured. He looked utterly drained as if the treatment had sapped every bit of his strength. Young Amane shyly presented the amulet she had made. Though the crooked writing seemed powerless, the deacon still grasped it firmly and carefully. "Sorry, I don't think I did a good job..." "Child, this amulet is the best in the world as long as your heart is sincere."

legacy:live:hero:yeonwoo:heroes.title: Yeonwoo
legacy:live:hero:yeonwoo:heroes.description: Yeonwoo is a passionate swordswoman, admired by all for her meticulous nature and sharp eye. She has an uncanny ability to see things from a unique perspective, likely due to her extensive travels and broadened horizons. Whether friend or foe, it is wise to always stay on high alert when you are around Yeonwoo. "Accomplishing something is hard, but ruining it is easy." This is the principle Yeonwoo has lived by her whole life. During her journeys, she saw many abandon their Convictions in pursuit of short-term gain. Most people understand the value of perseverance, but few truly practice it. "A blade must be honed a thousand times to be sharp, and a dance takes a lifetime of dedication to master." Yeonwoo weaves this principle of swordsmanship into every aspect of her daily life. Yeonwoo first held a sword at the age of five—a ceremonial blade that stood taller than she did. While other children were still busy playing and roughhousing, she rose early each morning, practicing her stance with quiet determination. She tirelessly repeated the routine day after day, each session lasting for a few hours. It wasn't until a year later that her master, who was also her father, finally taught her the most basic moves. At that moment, no one could have foreseen the remarkable things she would go on to achieve in the future. Yeonwoo trains in autumn to absorb the spirit of fallen petals and races through stormy nights to emulate the grace of swallows. She incorporates everything she has seen and heard into her dance. Each time she executes her moves, she reconnects with her beliefs and purpose. Each time she sheaths her sword, she quiets her restlessness with calm. Yeonwoo believes that the vast insights gained from her travels, intertwined with her skills, will one day give rise to the ultimate dance—one that embodies the heart and soul of the world.

legacy:live:hero:fahd:heroes.title: Fahd
legacy:live:hero:fahd:heroes.description: Fahd's armor glinted coldly in the wind as his eagle circled overhead, heralding the battle to come. As the weather grew harsher, visibility dropped to less than twenty meters. The sharp cry of the eagle set everyone on edge. "Fortunately, Fahd warned us beforehand," a frontline soldier muttered under his breath. "Otherwise, the enemy's sneak attack might have worked." Fahd kept his eyes fixed ahead and pressed his body low against his horse's back, unfazed by the biting wind and swirling sand. The black-clad c Avalry beside him mirrored his stance. As silence settled over the ranks, they prepared to launch their counterattack on the Ambushers. As the roar of battle waned and the Sandstorm subsided, the long-awaited sunlight finally filtered through the clouds. In the city, the ringing of bells and the cry of the eagle mingled with cheers of victory. The city mayor offered his riches as a gesture of gratitude, but Fahd firmly grasped his wrist and declined. "This is written in my fate, my friend. We didn't fight for wealth or fame." Bathed in the morning light amidst the crowd, Fahd wiped the dirt off his face. At that moment, the brave figure of this outlander was firmly etched into everyone's heart. Fahd may be merciless on the battlefield, but he is adored by the children in the city. Even Forrest the lumberjack counts himself as one of Fahd's biggest admirers, mostly thanks to his vivid storytelling. Some kids say Fahd has a magic box that could keep him telling stories for a thousand nights without running dry, but Fahd explains they are merely bedtime stories his mother told him when he was a child. His captivating stories are bound to take on a life of their own, traveling from crackling bonfires to children's eager ears. They will continue to wander far as those children grow up. Fahd's eagle plays a pivotal role in his military campaigns. Whenever a battle intensifies, it soars across the sky like a streak of lightning, offering his owner much-needed aid. Fahd's rapport with his eagle often gives him a strategic edge during battle. For example, three circles in the sky mean the eagle has spotted supplies; a sharp, urgent whistle calls it to patrol nearby; and a steep dive signals the enemy's location. What about the attack signal, which is the most important of all? That is a secret Fahd will never share with anyone.

legacy:live:hero:chenko:heroes.title: Chenko
legacy:live:hero:chenko:heroes.description: Chenko doesn't look like an inventor. Runaway, street urchin, or fugitive are the first possibilities that come to mind. Chenko also carries an enormous blunderbuss, also known by some as a "lightning stick". Pointing this terrifying weapon at someone gives Chenko more than enough leverage to ignore whatever threat anyone may make. Her strength depends on her skills as inventor, nothing more nothing less. And she is more than happy to test the effectiveness of her inventions on evildoers. Whenever the Rebels are at the gates, Chenko takes great joy in picking them off. If there are no Rebels? Dangerous predators will do just fine. There are those who counsel Chenko not to rely overmuch on her newfangled weapons. What if they suddenly fail in a fight? "Then my enemy might survive". Chenko's previous two prototypes were failures. The wealth that had funded her experiments in gunpowder projectiles was running out. Pressure was mounting. If Chenko haven't received her "lucky break" in the form of a Rebel attack during her third demonstration, it is quite likely she would have had to skip town altogether. Chenko was ready to demonstrate her new blunderbuss when the bell tower alarm sounded. Rebel cavalry were at the gates! "...This slender new weapon must be seen to be believed! Far more reliable than a traditional cannon, it will convince you on the first try, guaranteed! None can block the dark lightning that shoots out of the barrel. Invented by the brilliant Chenko, foremost prodigy of her age... No Governor can afford to be without this extremely reliable investment in their town defenses!" Chenko shook her head. She had paid two silver for the advertisement and yet its wording left something to be desired. "Feeling embarrassed by the weight of your armor? The short length of your sword? Here's an opportunity to solve all your problems with the most brilliant inventor, Chenko, you'll ever meet! Whether it's improving existing weapons or crafting new shields and armor, this is one master-crafter you can't afford to miss (assuming you have the funds). Get yourself down to the house at 3-6 G Street today!" So says the flyer in the royal museum. It must be decades old now, and a precious reminder of those early days when the inventor Chenko was not a household name.

legacy:live:hero:gordon:heroes.title: Gordon
legacy:live:hero:gordon:heroes.description: Gordon's work ethic is legendary. The governor once joked that if Gordon put up his feet for an afternoon that he would give him a silver coin for learning the "art of resting". Was this incentive enough? No. There are also rumors the governor will declare any holiday taken by Gordon a public holiday for the entire town, with all expenses paid for from the governor's pocket. What are we to make of these outlandish claims? Namely, that Gordon never stops working (or talking too, even in his sleep). Secondly, the governor's silver is quite safe from Gordon and the town's lack of public funds is quite safe from being exposed. No one from the old palace ever united public opinion (excluding the old king and General Cesares) quite like chef Gordon, whose signature recipes have been copied from coast to coast. But professional success doesn't necessarily translate to personal popularity. Outside of the kitchen Gordon is generally considered a foul-mouthed, sullen, and irritating perfectionist that has earned him the title "the mad chef". Not many people get to know the real Gordon underneath his rough exterior—except perhaps Howard, whom he once rescued from an imperial prison. Always at the top of any list ranking the kingdom's greatest chefs, and purveyor of 25 separate restaurants, Gordon somehow found time in his busy schedule to donate huge amounts of silver to the poor and look after the royal kitchen. If anyone can be called the pontiff of the cooking world, it's Gordon. Yet the same professional is also the fastest to lose his temper. In the kitchen he might be found at any point to be yelling curse words. "Get out of here, Jack! You call these steamed clams? I oughtta kick you out of the kitchen myself. Now get!" Gordon is also a man of righteous fury. Luckily, he is also pretty good with a spatula in a tight spot. Somehow Gordon didn't think twice about organizing a prison break for his friend Howard. His friend could only look at the unfolding drama and wonder: what manner of chef is this? Gordon brandished the spatula aggressively in the face of the prison guards. "Get back, scumbags!" he shouted. It was hard to get close to the flailing chef. Little by little, Gordon and his rescuee inched to the exit. It was hard to imagine a stranger sight than a middle-aged chef in an apron waving a spatula with a helpless friend under his other arm. Even stranger still is Gordon received barely a scratch for his jailbreak. The strangest part yet? His friend remained asleep through most of escape, wrapped up in a carpet...

legacy:live:hero:diana:heroes.title: Diana
legacy:live:hero:diana:heroes.description: Youngest member of the wilderness rangers cavalry group, Diana is famous inside and outside for her dashing red hair, good looks, steely-cold exterior, and fighting skills. Many are the soldiers of neighboring kingdoms who would love to be better acquainted with the red-haired maiden of the rangers. No matter Diana's reputation within the mercenary corps, she must still face the same the baptism of fire. Eventually she must face a Netherfiend. Alone. It is a mighty foe even to the most experienced warrior. Somewhere deep in the dark desert the Netherfiend roams, seeking an opportunity to attack travelers at their weakest point. It is this test more than any other that has come to vex Diana of late... Diana was first discovered by the wilderness rangers during a routine quest. Baby Diana was still swaddled in diapers and did not cry as most others would in that desolate place. The infant calmly gazed at the commander with her lovely eyes as he decided her fate. Without hesitation he picked her up and placed her on horseback. She would ride with them for death or glory. Karma was certainly in force that day. The commander expected many casualties and a difficult battle. Not even a hair of one of his regiment were harmed at the end of the fight. Was it a miracle? Had rescuing Diana brought good luck? It soon became something of a ritual for departing rangers to speak a few words to the child before departing for good luck. Diana's first solo mission came when she was still a teenager. For two days and nights she camped out near a swamp-infested watering hole. When the travelling bandit leader stopped for water, she slew him instantly. The young child has grown into quite the warrior with a patience and determination that surprises most people who see only her fair looks. She has become an immovable force within the mercenary unit, utterly devoted to her adoptive father and idealism of the rangers. "Every member of the rangers is free. Every member is part of a greater whole. Only three principles govern our every action. Follow these and you may call yourself a ranger without shame or challenge. Hold them fast to the last. Deny them and we shall deny you. First, never oppress the weak. Second, respect freedom of conscience. Never press another into your service. Third, there shall be no betrayal in our ranks. Even if you must lose your own life." The rangers' sacred tenets are never far from Diana's heart. On any other subject Diana will say little. Talk to her of the wilderness rangers and her eyes will light up and words flow like a mountain stream.

legacy:live:hero:howard:heroes.title: Howard
legacy:live:hero:howard:heroes.description: Distinguished guardsman of the Sixth Imperial Cavalry, Howard was used to putting his life on the line in defense of the emperor and his waystations, which soon earned him a promotion to auxiliary commander. His most glorious moment came during the Cesares Rebel invasion. Fortunately, his men held the line against the Rebels, protecting the waystations behind. Unfortunately, his was the only unit to do so... If there is one thing the unwieldy Imperial bureaucracy do not like it is people that make them look bad. A confused Howard found himself out of the Guards. But even this wasn't enough. An imperial warrant for his arrest soon showed up too. Imperial prisons are dirty, unpleasant places. Howard's only consolation was he became good friends with the chef, Gordon, who did his best to look after Howard as does best he could. What happened next would have been impossible without a friend on the inside. "Don't eat tonight's cookies" Gordon said innocently as he passed by Howard's cell. That night the guardsmen in Howard's block were excited to see extra cookies to go around. Thump! There were a series of loud bangs from the ground. What was going on? The last thing Howard remembered before losing consciousness was that he probably should have listened to Gordon's advice and not also eaten a cookie. Howard awoke to find himself wrapped up tightly in a coarse rug. Beside him was his gruff, stubble-faced chef friend who complained loudly about "all of that darned sleep-talking". "You don't like my pizza?!" "It's not stealing if it's in the recipe, is it?!" As Gordon kept walking Howard realized there was something different about the air here: it smelled of freedom. Thus Howard became chief sentry of the local village. The ex-army background made him qualified. But it is also a job that he cares about deeply. This, after all, is the village that saved his life. Howard's first test came quickly with a surprise Rebel attack. Without decent weapons, Howard's men were forced back to the old town fort which itself was barely hanging on by a thread. Chenko the "great inventor" ripped the door from its hinges and started hammering. Thereafter Howard became known as the guardian with the plank-shield and their village's most loyal defender.

legacy:live:hero:quinn:heroes.title: Quinn
legacy:live:hero:quinn:heroes.description: Quinn is a thrill-seeker abroad and hedonist at home, content to spend his days on wine and women while enjoying the occasional adventure. He has only one principle, and that is that everyone is ultimately on their own. Trying to rescue other people is a great way to get both of you hurt and, besides, why let others tie you down? Most men are impressed by Quinn's powerful figure, quick wit, and incredible skill with a crossbow. Women even more so. Some people are born charismatic and Quinn is one of them. He has an easygoing charm, a kind of magnetic quality to his gaze, a casual affability that conceals a careful purposefulness. An evening with Quinn can be quite the experience. "I think this is a task for me, fair lady. Allow me to assist!" "I must say, I am rather spellbound by your beauty, madam. Can I buy you a drink?" "I say, I see you have great talent, young master" "Honored governor, I would love it if you allowed me to entertain you for an evening? We have much to talk about concerning recent affairs of state." In short, Quinn will say whatever he thinks will charm and persuade others. Where is Quinn from? Nobody knows. A wanderer fleeing a powerful enemy? A man of the cloth for whom the temptation of vice became too great? Others, grasping at straws, guess Quinn was once an important member of stone-workers guild because of a strange masonry symbol on his crossbow. The only person who refuses to get involved in this speculation is Quinn himself. But that only adds to the mystique. There was once a senator from long ago in a republic far away who was expelled in great disgrace. Never mind the official reason, the truth had more to do with the senator's idealistic proposals around a kingdom-wide network of waystations and other stumbling blocks to the money-making schemes of those who ruled his city-state. Such foolishness had to be nipped in the bud. Reports of a fire spread throughout the capital. Where? The disgraced senator's villa. No one knows how many servants and household members lost their lives that day in the fire. Truthfully, no one wanted to know. It was better to remain apart, uninvolved. One could not risk staining one's own good name by association with one marked out of the senatorial rolls. Even the senator's name became taboo in polite company. It was a name so innocuous and yet afterward spoken with so much fear: Quinn.

legacy:live:hero:olive:heroes.title: Olive
legacy:live:hero:olive:heroes.description: War does strange things to people. Olive used to be an accomplished baker before the troubles. It was then she discovered her extraordinary talent for archery. War did not come easily to the gentle baker-turned-markswoman. Before the war, the only time Olive had ever so much as raised her voice was in response to troublesome customers. Olive's archery exploits have attracted plenty of attention, even rumors that she is of royal blood. She hails from a far northern land—that much is known. There is something striking about the rumor of a runaway princess. But these questions will not be answered for now. The last person she caught snooping had to be rescued by the Village Constable after a head injury. After that her admirers learned to focus on the present. If Olive has a best friend that must be Chenko, the only customer who actually seems to like what she stocks on the shelves. Olive's baking skills are a mixed bag for others. Either there's "too much flour", "too much water" or "not enough of either". As some of her critics are fond of saying: "Olive's bakery shows that staying hungry is always an option." North beyond the viking land stands the mighty Empire of Gold, symbolized by the emblem of curling golden flower buds. Said to be defended by great legions, a holy corps of warrior-priests, and ruled by an undying emperor of supreme knowledge and power, little has been heard of the empire for the last few decades. The sudden lack of news is rather mysterious. Is it any coincidence the southern lands have also recently seen an influx of proselytizers of a strange new sect?

legacy:live:hero:edwin:heroes.title: Edwin
legacy:live:hero:edwin:heroes.description: Edwin is an oddball, too intelligent to be considered a village idiot, but too strange for most to handle. A man of few words at work, the strong and silent mask drops as soon as he starts drinking. There he will entertain pubgoers with all manner of strange ideas. Strangeness is no great sin, particularly when paired with a steady stream of stones Edwin mines at the local quarry. Edwin doesn't have many friends anymore, not since the "accident". But those who used to know him will describe a dashing ladies' man with good looks and a muscular physique. All that changed, of course, after the mining disaster. Edwin, foreman of the team that was largely trapped down there, still feels partly responsible... "Help us! Help!" "Just hold on. I'm coming!" "Are you crazy? If you go down there, you're dead too!" "But I can't leave them!" "The storm has already moved the foundations! It's impossible. Just bad luck, Edwin." "Help us! Don't leave us down here to die, Edwin! Please!" "Relax. I'll do the report to the governor. Just make up a reason why it happened, OK? Don't worry, I'll make sure he knows it wasn't your fault." It was overcast. The sky had an ominous feel as the mine workers shuffled through the dense air as if wading through water. Foreman Edwin was still in bed. Last night's drinking had been a little heavy. As he slowly came to in the dormitory already crowded with men finishing the night shift, he thought he heard someone mutter "You know we could get a really big thunderstorm today." "Don't go!" Edwin sat up straight in bed with a yell, breathing heavily, nightshirt covered in sweat. The nightmare never truly left. But he was still determined to face whatever the day brought.

legacy:live:hero:seth:heroes.title: Seth
legacy:live:hero:seth:heroes.description: Seth is a smith. But despite that and the fact he spends most of his time in his smithy, metalworking is not his passion. No, what puts a spring in Seth's step is the thought of working on one of his many novels at the end of a long day. Will Seth carve out a successful life as a novelist? The resounding success of his short horror story "The Mysterious Case of the Missing Miner" indicates it is at least possible. Out of all of Seth's acquaintances who are literate, only Edwin disliked what he dismissively called "that penny dreadful garbage". That is promising. Seth's success with his first horror novel inspired his current magnum opus: "100 Years of Chaos"—a daring first-person account of the rise and fall of the Marquez Dynasty. For anyone privileged enough to read his first draft it is, by all accounts, a thrilling work of biting social commentary and high-minded ideals. What drives the humble blacksmith to feats of writing? "The long conversation of the soul," as he put it, "inspired by a friendship with an older man of the cloth who through long conversations on the power of the written word moved my younger self immensely". "Let me explain my journey with a dream I once had when I was younger. I felt like I was constantly searching for something in my room—I didn't know what. All I knew is I had to find it and I did! It was a page hidden deep within a pillow that told me to search for the First Holy Site... and in my dream, I found it. But then this hope of mine turned moldy and my ideals turned to dust. So I kept searching and then I found under my bed, the dying body of my younger self." "I am a firm believer that daylight will always come even if there is no sun! If you understand me, Pella, I believe you and I can both have confidence that a good day, a better day, will come." So writes Seth to one of his younger readers.

legacy:live:hero:forrest:heroes.title: Forrest
legacy:live:hero:forrest:heroes.description: Forrest looks every bit the villain. Standing two meters tall, the bald giant looms over other villagers, his beard and the jagged scar a typical sign of an outlaw. But that has also made Forrest the perfect go-to for dealing with the town's unruly children. A side-gig that has since come to complement his main trade: woodcutting. Alina's father died in the wars. Mother had to work late. Forrest wiped the sweat from his brow as he went out to look for her in the forest for the eighth time this month. His fingers found a few beautiful flowers as he searched. By the time Alina had been delivered to her waiting mother she had a little laurel courtesy of the friendly giant. Forrest wasn't quite sure why he did this. Who was it really for? "Thanks for bringing her back! Say, why don't you come in? Eat with us for once?" The friendly lady cropped her hair back as she waved hello. "Stay won't you, Uncle Forrest?! You know, Mom's soup is the best in the whole wide world!" It was hard to say no to Alina's tearfully optimistic face. "Next time maybe?" Forrest replied half-mumbling as his hands fidgeted nervously for something to do. Many years have passed since that day. Now Forrest, Alina and her mother are a family. The place where they live is an oasis of forest near a mountain that receives the first rays of the dawn sun. The trees of the mountain are well-sheltered by the towering peak just as the family are well-sheltered from the chaos of the outside world—by their survival skills and also the strong arms of the woodcutter.

legacy:live:item:transfer-passes:items.title: Transfer Passes

legacy:live:event:hall-of-governors:even.title: Hall of Governors
legacy:live:event:hall-of-governors:even.description: The Hall of Governors is a recurring competitive event in Kingshot that takes place during the first and second generations of a kingdom. This multi-day competition challenges players to complete specific objectives to earn points, unlock milestone rewards, and climb a regional leaderboard.

legacy:live:event:strongest-governor:eve.title: Strongest Governor
legacy:live:event:strongest-governor:eve.description: The Strongest Governor is a recurring competitive event in Kingshot , where players compete to earn points through various development and combat activities. It is one of the most important progression events in the game, offering valuable rewards including hero shards, resources, and exclusive items.

legacy:live:event:kingdom-of-power:event.title: Kingdom of Power
legacy:live:event:kingdom-of-power:event.description: Kingdom of Power (often called KvK, Kingdom vs Kingdom) is the most important event in Kingshot. Why? Because it is the only event where, if you win, you can essentially claim ownership of another kingdom.

legacy:live:event:alliance-brawl:events.title: Alliance Brawl
legacy:live:event:alliance-brawl:events.description: Alliance Brawl is a recurring 6.5-day alliance challenge where two alliances from different kingdoms face off for prestige, points, and exclusive rewards. The event begins right after the Kingdom of Power event in eligible kingdoms and often runs at the same time as the Merchant Empire event, and the armament/officer projects.

legacy:live:event:merchant-empire:events.title: Merchant Empire Event
legacy:live:event:merchant-empire:events.description: Merchant Empire is an event which happens every month alongside the Alliance Brawl event (unless your kingdom is not qualified for Alliance Brawl in which case it will be its own separate event). The Merchant Empire event usually occurs after the Kingdom of Power event. This event runs for 7 days in which only 6 of those days will allow the user to escort their caravans. During the 7th day you can still attack the enemy caravans albeit for only 4 hours.

legacy:live:event:champagne-fair:events.title: Champagne Fair
legacy:live:event:champagne-fair:events.description: Champagne Fair is a special two-day event in Kingshot. It unlocks after you complete the third Hall of Governors and returns about once per month. This event is one of the best ways to turn unused items into valuable materials.

legacy:live:event:hero-roulette:events.title: Roulette Hero
legacy:live:event:hero-roulette:events.description: A free to play’s best friend, and great source of Mythical Heroes! Have fun spinning a wheel, and claim/grow your Mythical Hero every 2 weeks!

legacy:live:event:viking-vengeance:event.title: Viking Vengeance

legacy:live:event:mystic-trial:events.title: Mystic Trial
legacy:live:event:mystic-trial:events.description: Mystic Trial is a permanent PvE feature with rotating zones, first-clear milestones, weekly raid rewards, and a Trial Crystal shop.

legacy:live:event:hall-of-heroes:events.title: Hall of Heroes
legacy:live:event:hall-of-heroes:events.description: Heroes will not be forgotten! All previous generations, both shards and widgets, can be found here. For current generations, only one of the three heroes will be available, no current generation widget! Great regular event for any player to improve on your heroes.

legacy:live:event:champions-way:events.title: Champion’s Way
legacy:live:event:champions-way:events.description: Champion’s Way is an event that takes the place of the Desert Trial Event in Generation 4. It works almost the same as Desert Trial, but the rewards are better, and you can unlock a specific Mythic Hero (Hilde in Gen 4). The event lasts for 3 days and returns every two weeks.

legacy:live:building:academy:buildings.description: ここは、都市のさまざまな要素を強化・発展させるための新たな技術を研究する場所です。 学院には、「発展」「経済」「戦闘」の3つのタブがあります。

legacy:live:building:barracks:buildings.title: 歩兵営舎
legacy:live:building:barracks:buildings.description: 歩兵の訓練およびアップグレード（昇格）を行う施設です。役場レベル7に達すると解放されます。 歩兵営舎は役場のレベルに応じて段階的に強化でき、通常、役場を次のレベルへ進めるための必要条件の1つとなります。施設をアップグレードするごとに、一度に訓練できる兵士の数（訓練容量）が増加し、訓練時間が短縮されるほか、自身の総力も上昇します。 また、特定のレベルに達することで、より高ランクの兵士（Tier）が解放されます。T5兵士（豪胆）を解放すると、それまでに訓練した低ランクの兵士を、現在訓練可能な最高ランクへと昇格させることができるようになります。 学院の「発展」タブにある技術「兵舎増設」を研究することでも、一度に訓練できる兵士の数をさらに増やすことができます。また、同じく「発展」タブにある「訓練機材」を研究すると、部隊の訓練に必要な時間が短縮されます。
